pk.context: 150 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A gabapentinoid cleared almost entirely unchanged by the kidneys, so its elimination tracks creatinine clearance.

clues.text: Oral bioavailability is at least 90% regardless of dose. It does not bind plasma proteins, is barely metabolized, and about 90% of a dose is recovered in urine unchanged.
Molecular weight 159.23. A crystalline solid, freely soluble in water, with pKa values of 4.2 and 10.6.
Approved under an NDA as capsules from 25 mg to 300 mg in eight strengths, and as a 20 mg/mL oral solution.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to it or its components; angioedema has occurred, and in children increased weight and appetite are among the most common reactions.
Neuropathic pain from diabetic neuropathy or spinal cord injury, postherpetic neuralgia, fibromyalgia, and adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures.
Binds with high affinity to the alpha 2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, but not directly to GABA or benzodiazepine receptors.
The generic name begins with P and has ten letters.
